name: Street Custom 'Lighthouse' Improvised Area Illumination Flare
product_name: Street Custom 'Lighthouse' Improvised Area Illumination Flare
description: A high-intensity chemical flare modified for area illumination rather than signaling — the Lighthouse produces 50,000 candela of white light for 5 minutes, illuminating a 100-meter radius bright enough to defeat low-light advantage. The flare is launched vertically by a hand-held tube launcher and descends slowly under a small parachute, bathing the area in light that negates night-vision equipment, thermal imaging (by raising ambient thermal signature), and the darkness that night operators depend on. It is the poor person's answer to tactical darkness advantage.
story_hooks: A night assault was defeated when defenders launched a dozen Lighthouse flares simultaneously — the attackers' night vision and thermal advantage was neutralized instantly, and they were exposed in bright white light to defenders behind cover.
Lighthouse flares have been modified with chemical additives that produce colored light — Tier 1 communities use them as emergency signals visible across districts.

physical_description.visual_profile: A cylindrical chemical flare cartridge with a stabilizing parachute pack mounted to its top. The body is a reinforced aluminum tube with a slightly tapered nose cone. The parachute housing forms a bulbous cap above the flare body, with deployment lines visible along the sides. Utilitarian and purposeful — designed for function over aesthetics.
physical_description.dimensions: Flare cartridge 12cm long, 4cm diameter; parachute housing adds 6cm height; total loaded length approximately 18cm
physical_description.weight_description: 400 grams per flare — handheld, fits in a tactical pouch or cargo pocket; light enough for rapid deployment
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum tube body; composite parachute canister; steel deployment springs
physical_description.finish: Matte anodize with visible machining marks; weathered from street use; minor oxidation stains visible on lower sections
physical_description.color_scheme: Dull steel-gray body with orange warning bands around the base; white stenciled labels and ignition instructions; red deployment-pull ring
physical_description.interface_elements: Friction-grip pull ring at base; pressure-activated ignition switch recessed into the cap; safety pin securing parachute deployment mechanism; printed ignition countdown timer and safety warnings in multiple languages
distinctive_features: Small perforated cooling vents running the length of the cartridge body
Factory-spray yellow chevron warning marks indicating upward-pointing orientation
Handwritten street modifications: wire wrapping around the base for reinforcement, crude solder joints where owners have replaced deployment springs
Parachute compartment lid features improvised adhesive patches from repair tape
Residual burn residue and scorch marks from previous test fires
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Street Custom logo (stylized lighthouse beam silhouette) stamped into aluminum; manufacturing date code; batch number; regulatory compliance stamp showing GLMZ safety certification; small print warning about eye damage and night-vision equipment interference
physical_description.condition_typical: Used units show handling wear — scuffed anodizing, slight dents from carrying, oxidation patina. Pristine versions appear too sterile for street work. Most users carry 2-3 in a bandolier across their chest or in drop-leg tactical pouches
